19
RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday, the December 5, 2003/Agrahayana 14, 1925 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Environment and
Forests; Food Processing Industries; Human Resource
Development; Ocean Development; Railways;
Science and Technology; Steel; Youth
Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions—20
Drought in  Southern States
*61. DR. DASARI NARAYANA
RAO:
SHRI K. B. KRISHNA
MURTHY:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that almost all
the Southern States  particularly Karnataka
and Kerala are in the grip of worst drought
this year;
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
(c) whether any Central team has visited
the States to assess the drought situation
there;
(d) if so, the findings thereof; and
(e) what relief measures have been
extended to the affected States so far,
State-wise?
Air-pollution in metros
†*62.  SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR: Will
the Minister of EN VIRONMENT AND
FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
air-pollution is increasing day by day in
the four metropolitan cities i.e. Delhi,
Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the date of the last study on pollution
in each of these metros;
(d) whether any fresh study is proposed
to be conducted; and
(e) whether any time-bound programme
has been prepared to reduce pollution and
if so, the details thereof?
ADB funds for Railway projects
*63. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fa ct that the Asian
Development Bank has agreed to Fund
some Railway projects;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

20
(b) if so, the details of the projects;
(c) the quantum of the assistance being
extended by the ADB; and
(d) the list of the externally aided
projects and details of the loan taken from
various agencies other than ADB?
Education for All-Global
monitoring report
*64. PROF. SAIF-UD-DIN SOZ:
 DR. MANMOHAN SINGH:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether he is aware of the fact that
UNESCO's latest Education For All (EFA)
global monitoring report says that
Bangladesh has achieved gender parity equal
enrolment of boys and girls at school at the
Primary level and India scraps the
bottom of the list just a little above
Pakistan; and
(b) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto?
Objectives of National Education
Policy
*65. DR. MANMOHAN SINGH: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the trend of public expenditure on
education expressed as a percentage of GDP
and total public expenditure since 1990;
and
(b) whether this trend is consistent with
the resource requirements for
meeting the National Education Policy
objectives?
Mid-Day Meal Scheme
*66. SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Mid-Day Meal Scheme has
been expanded  further throughout the
country;
(b) if so, whether many opposition
parties have also urged Centre to expand
Mid-Day Meal Scheme;
(c) whether mid-day meal supplied in
Delhi and other places have been found
affecting children instead of helping them;
(d) if so, whether Centre has been
informed that in number of States, after
mid-day meal were supplied, number of
children had been forced to go to hospitals;
(e) the total number of students who
were affected due to this; and
(f) the steps Government propose to
take to prevent such incidents in future?
Degrees to students of G.S.B.A.,
Greater Noida
*67. SHRI RAMA SHANKER
KAUSHIK: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to refer to  answers to Unstarred
Question 2824 and 4737 given in Rajya
Sabha on the 17th August, 2001 and 10th
May, 2002 respectively and state:
(a) the reasons for delay in awarding
'Degrees' to successful students who have
already completed the Masters in
Computer Application course in July, 2003
in the 'Approved' institute at Graduate
School of Business Administration, Greater
Noida;

21
(b) the details of steps initiated/likely
to be taken to honour the commitments
already made by Visva Bharti,
Shantiniketan to safeguard the interests of
successful students of the batch passing
out in July, 2003 already enrolled at
Graduate School of  Business
Administration, Greater Noida; and
(c) by when, the final Marks Statement
and Degree Certificates are likely to be
issued to them?
Expansion and growth of FPIs
†*68. SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH
'LALAN':
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have taken a
decision to implement a time-bound scheme
for expansion and growth of food
processing industry in the country so that
fruits and vegetables worth Rs. 50,000 crore
could be saved from being perished without
being used;
(b) if so, the scheme of the Government
in this

RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday, the December 5, 2003/Agrahayana 14, 1925 (Saka)
————
(Ministries :  Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Environment and
Forests; Food Processing Industries; Human Resource Development;
Ocean Development; Railways; Science and Technology; Steel;
Youth Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions—143
Price support for saffron crop
342. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the fact that for the first time in four years,
Kishtwar’s saffron farmers are expecting a
good saffron crop;
(b) if so, whether Government have
noticed the fact that official neglect has hit
the farmers' interests hard and they rarely
get the attention and the prices they deserve;
and
(c) if so, the efforts, Government
propose  to make the Government-run
price support mechanism available for the
benefit of such farmers?
Assistance to Andhra Pradesh
from NCCF
343. DR. ALLADI P. RAJKUMAR:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Andhra Pradesh
Assembly has passed a unanimous
resolution requesting the Central
Government to immediately release
Rs. 996.12 crores from National
Calamity Contingency Fund and 15 lakh
tonnes of rice under the Swarna Jayanti
Grameen Rozgar Yojana to meet the need
of drought affected areas of the
State; and
(b) if so, the response of the Central
Government in this regard?
Promotion of organic farming
344. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that
Government have formulated a national
project on organic farming with an outlay
of Rs. 99.58 crore to improve the soil
health;
(b) whether the project envisages the
setting up of National Institute of Organic
Farming (NIOF) for the production,
promotion, market development and
regulation of organic farming in the country;
and
(c) if so, the details of the proposed
scheme?

76
Agriculture research and education
centres
345. SHRI SK. KHABIR UDDIN
AHMED: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to refer to
answer to Unstarred Question 1343, given
in the Rajya Sabha on the 1st August, 2003
and state:
(a) the details of basic infrastructure
provided by the agriculture research and
education centres; and
(b) the steps taken by Government to
upgrade these research centres?
Insurance cover for yield and
price fluctuations
346. SHRI NANA DESHMUKH: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
introduce a new insurance cover for yield
and price fluctuations for farmers under a
single policy;
(b) if so, the details of the scheme; and
(c) by when it is likely to be put in
operation?
Assistance to SC/ST farmers of
M.P.
347. SHRI P.K. MAHESHWARI: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to release the fund from the contingency
fund to help the SCs/STs and Backward
agriculturists in Madhya Pradesh;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Assistance to pest affected
district Malkangiri, Orissa
348. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that over 5000
families of farmers in the tribal dominated
Malkangiri district of Orissa were in
distress, on account of pest attacks on their
crops which had, in turn, affected their
livelihood; and
(b) whether the Centre has offered
assistance to the cash-strapped State to
compensate the affected farmers; if so, the
details thereof?
All day milk stalls of DMS
349. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there are many DMS outlets
running in Delhi by the name of 'All Day
Milk Stalls’;
(b) if so, whether these outlets have been
opened as franchisee of DMS;
(c) if so, the number of outlets that are
running in Delhi; and
(d) the amount of revenue earned by
DMS as franchise deposits?
Survey of wheat varieties
350. MISS MABEL REBELLO: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a survey of
wheat varieties suitable for overseas market
as well as for better yield is being conducted;
(b) if so, the result of such exercise;

77
(c) by when Government propose to
introduce such varieties for commercial
production; and
(d) the details thereof?
Boosting sale of DMS milk
351. SHRI MURLI DEORA: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) the percentage of milk in polypacks
returned to Delhi Milk Scheme during the
last three years, year-wise;
(b) the additional expenditure incurred
in reprocessing of these polypacks;
(c) whether the sale of milk had
decreased as a result of increase in prices
and if so, the action taken to reduce it and
boosting the sale; and
(d) the distribution losses reported
during the last three years?
Shortage of milk in Delhi

Minister of AGRICULTU
